C.3 Forget Lock Characterization

Proposition C.6 (Forget Lock Characterization).

Let Πu,μ=Bu,μ​(Bu,μ)⊤\Pi_{u,\mu}=B_{u,\mu}(B_{u,\mu})^{\top} be the orthogonal projector onto 𝒰μ\mathcal{U}_{\mu}. Then ℒf​(w)=0\mathcal{L}_{f}(w)=0 if and only if Πu,μ​(wμ−wn,μ)=0\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}-w_{n,\mu})=0 for both μ∈{v,t}\mu\in\{v,t\}. Moreover, ∇wμℒf=2​Πu,μ​(wμ−wn,μ)\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{f}=2\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}-w_{n,\mu}), which vanishes for displacements orthogonal to 𝒰μ\mathcal{U}_{\mu} and points back toward wn,μw_{n,\mu} along 𝒰μ\mathcal{U}_{\mu} otherwise.

Proof.

Since the two modalities contribute independently, it suffices to analyze a single modality μ\mu. Let Δμ=wμ−wn,μ\Delta_{\mu}=w_{\mu}-w_{n,\mu}. The μ\mu-th summand of ℒf\mathcal{L}_{f} can be expanded as

ℓμ=Δμ⊤​Πu,μ​Δμ=Δμ⊤​Bu,μ​(Bu,μ)⊤​Δμ=‖(Bu,μ)⊤​Δμ‖22≥ 0.\begin{split}\ell_{\mu}&=\Delta_{\mu}^{\top}\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{\mu}\\ &=\Delta_{\mu}^{\top}B_{u,\mu}(B_{u,\mu})^{\top}\Delta_{\mu}\\ &=\bigl\|(B_{u,\mu})^{\top}\Delta_{\mu}\bigr\|_{2}^{2}\;\geq\;0.\end{split} (19)

Therefore ℓμ=0\ell_{\mu}=0 if and only if

(Bu,μ)⊤​Δμ=0⟺Δμ∈𝒰μ⟂⟺Πu,μ​Δμ=0.(B_{u,\mu})^{\top}\Delta_{\mu}=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Delta_{\mu}\in\mathcal{U}_{\mu}^{\perp}\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{\mu}=0. (20)

Summing over both modalities, ℒf​(w)=0\mathcal{L}_{f}(w)=0 iff Πu,μ​(wμ−wn,μ)=0\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}-w_{n,\mu})=0 for both μ∈{v,t}\mu\in\{v,t\}. Since Πu,μ\Pi_{u,\mu} is symmetric and wn,μw_{n,\mu} is constant, the standard identity ∇x(x⊤​A​x)=2​A​x\nabla_{x}(x^{\top}A\,x)=2A\,x gives

∇wμℒf=∇wμ[Δμ⊤​Πu,μ​Δμ]=2​Πu,μ​Δμ=2​Πu,μ​(wμ−wn,μ).\begin{split}\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{f}&=\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\bigl[\Delta_{\mu}^{\top}\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{\mu}\bigr]\\ &=2\,\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{\mu}\\ &=2\,\Pi_{u,\mu}\,(w_{\mu}-w_{n,\mu}).\end{split} (21)

This gradient lies in 𝒰μ=im⁡(Πu,μ)\mathcal{U}_{\mu}=\mathrm{im}(\Pi_{u,\mu}) and vanishes iff Δμ∈𝒰μ⟂\Delta_{\mu}\in\mathcal{U}_{\mu}^{\perp}. ∎

C.4 Proof of Theorem C.7 (Unlearning Completeness)

Theorem C.7 (Unlearning Completeness).

Let wμ∗w_{\mu}^{*} denote the projected parameters and Δμ=wμ−wn,μ\Delta_{\mu}=w_{\mu}-w_{n,\mu} the pre-projection displacement. Then:

  1. (i)

    Exact erasure: Πu,μ​(wμ∗−wn,μ)=0\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}^{*}-w_{n,\mu})=0, i.e., the projected displacement has zero component along 𝒰μ\mathcal{U}_{\mu}.

  2. (ii)

    Energy removal: The energy removed equals ‖Πu,μ​Δμ‖22\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\Delta_{\mu}\|_{2}^{2}. For any Δμ∈𝒮f\Delta_{\mu}\in\mathcal{S}_{f} expressed in the canonical basis as Δμ=∑i=1pαi​ci\Delta_{\mu}=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}c_{i}, this equals ∑i:cos⁡φi≤δαi2\sum_{i:\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta}\alpha_{i}^{2}.

  3. (iii)

    Forget energy ratio: ηf​(δ)=‖Bu,μ⊤​Gf,μ‖F2/‖Gf,μ‖F2\eta_{f}(\delta)=\|B_{u,\mu}^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}/\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2} is monotonically non-decreasing in δ\delta and satisfies ηf​(1)≥τe\eta_{f}(1)\geq\tau_{e} (equality only when the truncation exactly meets the energy threshold).

Proof.

We work with a single modality μ\mu throughout; the argument applies identically to both branches. Let Δμ=wμ−wn,μ\Delta_{\mu}=w_{\mu}-w_{n,\mu} denote the pre-projection displacement.

We begin by establishing exact erasure. By Eq. (10), the projected parameters satisfy wμ∗=wμ−Πu,μ​Δμw_{\mu}^{*}=w_{\mu}-\Pi_{u,\mu}\Delta_{\mu}. Subtracting wn,μw_{n,\mu} from both sides and applying Πu,μ\Pi_{u,\mu}:

Πu,μ​(wμ∗−wn,μ)=Πu,μ​[Δμ−Πu,μ​Δμ]=Πu,μ​(Idμ−Πu,μ)​Δμ=(Πu,μ−Πu,μ2)​Δμ=(Πu,μ−Πu,μ)​Δμ=0,\begin{split}\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}^{*}-w_{n,\mu})&=\Pi_{u,\mu}\bigl[\Delta_{\mu}-\Pi_{u,\mu}\Delta_{\mu}\bigr]\\ &=\Pi_{u,\mu}\,(I_{d_{\mu}}-\Pi_{u,\mu})\,\Delta_{\mu}\\ &=(\Pi_{u,\mu}-\Pi_{u,\mu}^{2})\,\Delta_{\mu}\\ &=(\Pi_{u,\mu}-\Pi_{u,\mu})\,\Delta_{\mu}=0,\end{split} (22)

where the last line uses idempotency Πu,μ2=Πu,μ\Pi_{u,\mu}^{2}=\Pi_{u,\mu} (Proposition C.5).

Next, we quantify the energy removed by the projection. The squared norm of the removed component is

‖Δμ−(wμ∗−wn,μ)‖22=‖Δμ−(Idμ−Πu,μ)​Δμ‖22=‖Πu,μ​Δμ‖22.\begin{split}\|\Delta_{\mu}-(w_{\mu}^{*}-w_{n,\mu})\|_{2}^{2}&=\|\Delta_{\mu}-(I_{d_{\mu}}-\Pi_{u,\mu})\Delta_{\mu}\|_{2}^{2}\\ &=\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{\mu}\|_{2}^{2}.\end{split} (23)

Now suppose Δμ∈𝒮f\Delta_{\mu}\in\mathcal{S}_{f} and write Δμ=∑i=1pαi​ui\Delta_{\mu}=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}\,u_{i} in the canonical basis {ui}i=1p={(Φf​U)⋅,i}i=1p\{u_{i}\}_{i=1}^{p}=\{(\Phi_{f}U)_{\cdot,i}\}_{i=1}^{p}. Since {ui}\{u_{i}\} are orthonormal and Πu,μ\Pi_{u,\mu} projects onto span⁡{ui:cos⁡φi≤δ}\mathrm{span}\{u_{i}:\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta\}, we have Πu,μ​ui=ui\Pi_{u,\mu}\,u_{i}=u_{i} if cos⁡φi≤δ\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta and Πu,μ​ui=0\Pi_{u,\mu}\,u_{i}=0 otherwise. Therefore

‖Πu,μ​Δμ‖22=‖Πu,μ​∑i=1pαi​ui‖22=∥∑i:cos⁡φi≤δαiui∥22=∑i:cos⁡φi≤δαi2.\begin{split}\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{\mu}\|_{2}^{2}&=\Bigl\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}\,u_{i}\Bigr\|_{2}^{2}\\ &=\Bigl\|\sum_{i:\,\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta}\alpha_{i}\,u_{i}\Bigr\|_{2}^{2}\\ &=\sum_{i:\,\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta}\alpha_{i}^{2}.\end{split} (24)

Finally, we analyze the monotonicity of the forget energy ratio ηf​(δ)=‖Bu,μ⊤​Gf,μ‖F2/‖Gf,μ‖F2\eta_{f}(\delta)=\|B_{u,\mu}^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}/\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}. As δ\delta increases, the index set ℐu​(δ)={i:cos⁡φi≤δ}\mathcal{I}_{u}(\delta)=\{i:\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta\} can only grow, so Bu,μB_{u,\mu} gains columns and ‖Bu,μ⊤​Gf,μ‖F2\|B_{u,\mu}^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2} is non-decreasing in δ\delta. At δ=1\delta=1, all pp canonical directions are classified as removable anchor directions, so Bu,μ=Φf​UB_{u,\mu}=\Phi_{f}U. The boundary value evaluates as

ηf​(1)=‖Bu,μ⊤​Gf,μ‖F2‖Gf,μ‖F2=‖(Φf​U)⊤​Gf,μ‖F2‖Gf,μ‖F2=‖U⊤​Φf⊤​Gf,μ‖F2‖Gf,μ‖F2=‖Φf⊤​Gf,μ‖F2‖Gf,μ‖F2=∑i=1pσi2‖Gf,μ‖F2≥τe,\begin{split}\eta_{f}(1)&=\frac{\|B_{u,\mu}^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}{\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}=\frac{\|(\Phi_{f}U)^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}{\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}\\ &=\frac{\|U^{\top}\Phi_{f}^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}{\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}=\frac{\|\Phi_{f}^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}{\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sigma_{i}^{2}}{\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}}\geq\tau_{e},\end{split} (25)

where the fourth equality uses the orthogonality of UU (which preserves the Frobenius norm), and the last inequality follows from the energy criterion (6), which selects pp as the smallest index whose cumulative energy already reaches τe\tau_{e}. Equality holds only in special cases, e.g., when the truncation point exactly meets the threshold (∑i=1pσi2/‖Gf,μ‖F2=τe\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sigma_{i}^{2}/\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}=\tau_{e}) or when the retained principal directions span the entire column space of Gf,μG_{f,\mu} (so that p=rank⁡(Gf,μ)p=\mathrm{rank}(G_{f,\mu}) and ηf​(1)=1\eta_{f}(1)=1). ∎

C.5 Proof of Theorem C.8 (Retention Integrity)

Theorem C.8 (Retention Integrity).

For any retain displacement Δr∈𝒮r\Delta_{r}\in\mathcal{S}_{r}, the collateral energy is bounded by

‖Πu,μ​Δr‖22≤δ2​‖Δr‖22.\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{r}\|_{2}^{2}\;\leq\;\delta^{2}\,\|\Delta_{r}\|_{2}^{2}. (26)
Proof.

Let Δr∈𝒮r\Delta_{r}\in\mathcal{S}_{r} with ‖Δr‖2=1\|\Delta_{r}\|_{2}=1 (the general case follows by homogeneity). Express Δr\Delta_{r} in the canonical coordinate system of 𝒮r\mathcal{S}_{r}:

Δr=∑j=1qβj​vj+Δr⟂,\Delta_{r}=\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}\,v_{j}+\Delta_{r}^{\perp}, (27)

where vj=(Φr​V)⋅,jv_{j}=(\Phi_{r}V)_{\cdot,j} are the retain-side canonical directions, ∑jβj2+‖Δr⟂‖22=1\sum_{j}\beta_{j}^{2}+\|\Delta_{r}^{\perp}\|_{2}^{2}=1, and Δr⟂∈𝒮r∩span​(v1,…,vmin⁡(p,q))⟂\Delta_{r}^{\perp}\in\mathcal{S}_{r}\cap\mathrm{span}(v_{1},\dots,v_{\min(p,q)})^{\perp}.

By the canonical-angle property, ⟨ui,vj⟩=δi​jcosφi\langle u_{i},v_{j}\rangle=\delta_{ij}\cos\varphi_{i} for i≤min⁡(p,q)i\leq\min(p,q), and ⟨ui,Δr⟂⟩=0\langle u_{i},\Delta_{r}^{\perp}\rangle=0 for all ii since Δr⟂\Delta_{r}^{\perp} is orthogonal to all canonical directions that overlap with 𝒮f\mathcal{S}_{f}. Therefore, for each removable anchor direction uiu_{i} with cos⁡φi≤δ\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta:

⟨ui,Δr⟩=∑j=1qβj⟨ui,vj⟩+⟨ui,Δr⟂⟩=βicosφi+0=βicosφi.\langle u_{i},\Delta_{r}\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}\,\langle u_{i},v_{j}\rangle+\langle u_{i},\Delta_{r}^{\perp}\rangle=\beta_{i}\cos\varphi_{i}+0=\beta_{i}\cos\varphi_{i}. (28)

Summing over all removable anchor directions yields

‖Πu,μ​Δr‖22=∑i:cos⁡φi≤δ⟨ui,Δr⟩2=∑i:cos⁡φi≤δβi2cos2φi≤δ2∑i:cos⁡φi≤δβi2≤δ2​∑j=1qβj2≤δ2​‖Δr‖22,\begin{split}\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\,\Delta_{r}\|_{2}^{2}&=\sum_{i:\,\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta}\langle u_{i},\Delta_{r}\rangle^{2}\\ &=\sum_{i:\,\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta}\beta_{i}^{2}\,\cos^{2}\varphi_{i}\\ &\leq\delta^{2}\sum_{i:\,\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta}\beta_{i}^{2}\\ &\leq\delta^{2}\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}^{2}\\ &\leq\delta^{2}\,\|\Delta_{r}\|_{2}^{2},\end{split} (29)

where the first inequality uses cos⁡φi≤δ\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta for each removable anchor direction, and the last inequality uses ∑jβj2≤‖Δr‖22=1\sum_{j}\beta_{j}^{2}\leq\|\Delta_{r}\|_{2}^{2}=1. ∎

C.6 Completeness–Integrity Trade-off Analysis

The threshold δ\delta simultaneously controls the unlearning completeness ratio ηf​(δ)\eta_{f}(\delta) and the retention damage bound ηr​(δ)\eta_{r}(\delta). We formalize their joint behavior.

Proposition C.9 (Monotonicity and Pareto Trade-off).

Let ηf​(δ)=‖Bu,μ⊤​Gf,μ‖F2/‖Gf,μ‖F2\eta_{f}(\delta)=\|B_{u,\mu}^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}/\|G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2} and ηr​(δ)=maxΔr∈𝒮r∖{0}⁡‖Πu,μ​Δr‖22/‖Δr‖22\eta_{r}(\delta)=\max_{\Delta_{r}\in\mathcal{S}_{r}\setminus\{0\}}\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\Delta_{r}\|_{2}^{2}/\|\Delta_{r}\|_{2}^{2}. Then both ηf​(δ)\eta_{f}(\delta) and ηr​(δ)\eta_{r}(\delta) are monotonically non-decreasing in δ∈[0,1]\delta\in[0,1]. Moreover, for any target unlearning ratio ηf∗∈(0,τe]\eta_{f}^{*}\in(0,\tau_{e}], the smallest threshold achieving ηf​(δ)≥ηf∗\eta_{f}(\delta)\geq\eta_{f}^{*} is δ∗=cos⁡φk∗\delta^{*}=\cos\varphi_{k^{*}}, where k∗=min⁡{k:ηf​(cos⁡φk)≥ηf∗}k^{*}=\min\{k:\eta_{f}(\cos\varphi_{k})\geq\eta_{f}^{*}\} and φ1≤⋯≤φp\varphi_{1}\leq\dots\leq\varphi_{p} are the principal angles in non-decreasing order. This δ∗\delta^{*} simultaneously minimizes the retention damage bound (δ∗)2(\delta^{*})^{2}.

Proof.

We first establish monotonicity. For ηf\eta_{f}, as δ\delta increases, the index set ℐu​(δ)={i:cos⁡φi≤δ}\mathcal{I}_{u}(\delta)=\{i:\cos\varphi_{i}\leq\delta\} can only grow. Since Bu,μB_{u,\mu} is formed by collecting the columns of Φf​U\Phi_{f}U indexed by ℐu​(δ)\mathcal{I}_{u}(\delta), the projection Bu,μ⊤​Gf,μB_{u,\mu}^{\top}G_{f,\mu} captures a non-decreasing share of the forget gradient energy:

δ′>δ⟹ℐu​(δ)⊆ℐu​(δ′)⟹‖Bu,μ​(δ)⊤​Gf,μ‖F2≤‖Bu,μ​(δ′)⊤​Gf,μ‖F2,\delta^{\prime}>\delta\;\Longrightarrow\;\mathcal{I}_{u}(\delta)\subseteq\mathcal{I}_{u}(\delta^{\prime})\;\Longrightarrow\;\|B_{u,\mu}(\delta)^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}\;\leq\;\|B_{u,\mu}(\delta^{\prime})^{\top}G_{f,\mu}\|_{F}^{2}, (30)

so ηf​(δ)\eta_{f}(\delta) is non-decreasing. For ηr\eta_{r}: by Theorem C.8, ηr​(δ)≤δ2\eta_{r}(\delta)\leq\delta^{2}, and the bound δ2\delta^{2} is strictly increasing. More precisely,

ηr​(δ)=maxi∈ℐu​(δ)⁡cos2⁡φi,\eta_{r}(\delta)=\max_{i\in\mathcal{I}_{u}(\delta)}\cos^{2}\varphi_{i}, (31)

which is non-decreasing since ℐu​(δ)\mathcal{I}_{u}(\delta) grows with δ\delta.

Turning to the optimal threshold, we observe that ηf\eta_{f} is a step function that jumps only at the principal-angle cosines cos⁡φ1,…,cos⁡φp\cos\varphi_{1},\dots,\cos\varphi_{p}. Therefore, the smallest δ\delta achieving ηf​(δ)≥ηf∗\eta_{f}(\delta)\geq\eta_{f}^{*} must coincide with one of these cosines:

δ∗=cos⁡φk∗,k∗=min⁡{k:ηf​(cos⁡φk)≥ηf∗}.\delta^{*}=\cos\varphi_{k^{*}},\quad k^{*}=\min\bigl\{k:\eta_{f}(\cos\varphi_{k})\geq\eta_{f}^{*}\bigr\}. (32)

Among all δ\delta satisfying the constraint, δ∗\delta^{*} is minimal by construction. Since ηr≤δ2\eta_{r}\leq\delta^{2} is increasing in δ\delta, this δ∗\delta^{*} simultaneously minimizes the retention damage bound (δ∗)2(\delta^{*})^{2}. ∎

C.7 Proof of Theorem C.10 (Unlearning Durability)

Theorem C.10 (Unlearning Durability).

Suppose ‖Πu,μ​∇wμℒa‖2≤Gu\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}\|_{2}\leq G_{u} for all ww encountered during training and ηlr<1/(2​α)\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}<1/(2\alpha). The Temporal Re-anchoring drift after tt steps from the projected point obeys

‖Πu,μ​(wμ​(t)−wn,μ)‖2≤Gu2​α​[1−(1−2​ηlr​α)t]≤Gu2​α.\|\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}(t)-w_{n,\mu})\|_{2}\;\leq\;\frac{G_{u}}{2\alpha}\,\bigl[1-(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha)^{t}\bigr]\;\leq\;\frac{G_{u}}{2\alpha}. (33)
Proof.

Fix modality μ\mu and let d⁡(t)=Πu,μ​(wμ​(t)−wn,μ)d(t)=\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}(t)-w_{n,\mu}) denote the unique-subspace displacement at step tt. A single SGD step under the combined objective (12) updates:

wμ​(t+1)=wμ​(t)−ηlr​[∇wμℒa​(w⁡(t))+2​α​Πu,μ​(wμ​(t)−wn,μ)].w_{\mu}(t{+}1)=w_{\mu}(t)-\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\bigl[\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}(w(t))+2\alpha\,\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}(t)-w_{n,\mu})\bigr]. (34)

Applying Πu,μ\Pi_{u,\mu} to both sides and writing gu​(t)=Πu,μ​∇wμℒa​(w⁡(t))g_{u}(t)=\Pi_{u,\mu}\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}(w(t)):

d⁡(t+1)=Πu,μ​[wμ​(t+1)−wn,μ]=Πu,μ​(wμ​(t)−wn,μ)−ηlr​Πu,μ​∇wμℒa−2​ηlr​α​Πu,μ2​(wμ​(t)−wn,μ)=d⁡(t)−ηlr​gu​(t)−2​ηlr​α​d​(t)=(1−2​ηlr​α)​d​(t)−ηlr​gu​(t),\begin{split}d(t{+}1)&=\Pi_{u,\mu}\bigl[w_{\mu}(t{+}1)-w_{n,\mu}\bigr]\\ &=\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}(t)-w_{n,\mu})-\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,\Pi_{u,\mu}\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha\,\Pi_{u,\mu}^{2}(w_{\mu}(t)-w_{n,\mu})\\ &=d(t)-\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{u}(t)-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha\,d(t)\\ &=(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha)\,d(t)-\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{u}(t),\end{split} (35)

where ‖gu​(t)‖2≤Gu\|g_{u}(t)\|_{2}\leq G_{u} by assumption. Taking norms and applying the triangle inequality:

‖d⁡(t+1)‖2≤(1−2​ηlr​α)​‖d⁡(t)‖2+ηlr​Gu.\|d(t{+}1)\|_{2}\;\leq\;(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha)\,\|d(t)\|_{2}+\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,G_{u}. (36)

Since ηlr<1/(2​α)\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}<1/(2\alpha), the contraction factor γ=1−2​ηlr​α∈(0,1)\gamma=1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha\in(0,1). Starting from ‖d⁡(0)‖2=0\|d(0)\|_{2}=0 (exact erasure by Theorem C.7), unrolling the recurrence gives:

‖d⁡(t)‖2≤ηlr​Gu​∑s=0t−1γs=ηlr​Gu​(1−γt)1−γ=Gu2​α​[1−(1−2​ηlr​α)t].\begin{split}\|d(t)\|_{2}&\leq\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}G_{u}\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\gamma^{s}\\ &=\frac{\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}G_{u}\,(1-\gamma^{t})}{1-\gamma}\\ &=\frac{G_{u}}{2\alpha}\,\bigl[1-(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha)^{t}\bigr].\end{split} (37)

Since (1−2​ηlr​α)t≥0(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\alpha)^{t}\geq 0, the bound is at most Gu/(2​α)G_{u}/(2\alpha). ∎

C.8 Proof of Theorem C.11 (Anchor Reconstruction Tendency under Unilateral Excision)

Theorem C.11 (Anchor Reconstruction Tendency under Unilateral Excision).

Under Assumptions A1–A4 (Appendix C.1), suppose excision is applied to modality μ\mu only, producing wμ∗w_{\mu}^{*} with Πu,μ​(wμ∗−wn,μ)=0\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}^{*}-w_{n,\mu})=0, while wμ¯w_{\bar{\mu}} is held at wn,μ¯w_{n,\bar{\mu}}. Define the Modality Anchor signal along the unique subspace at the excised point as g0:=‖Πu,μ​∇wμℒa​(wμ∗,wn,μ¯)‖2g_{0}:=\|\Pi_{u,\mu}\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}(w_{\mu}^{*},w_{n,\bar{\mu}})\|_{2}. Then:

  1. (i)

    Anchor survives (A1–A2): g0>0g_{0}>0 whenever the anchor embedding zμ¯​(wn,μ¯)z_{\bar{\mu}}(w_{n,\bar{\mu}}) has a non-zero component along the range of Jμ​(wμ∗)⊤J_{\mu}(w_{\mu}^{*})^{\top} restricted to 𝒰μ\mathcal{U}_{\mu}.

  2. (ii)

    Drift lower-bound tendency (A1–A2, A4): one local SGD step on the retain objective gives ‖Πu,μ​(wμ​(1)−wn,μ)‖2≥ηlr​g0\|\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}(1)-w_{n,\mu})\|_{2}\geq\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{0}. Under the alignment condition A4, for step ηlr<1/(2​L)\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}<1/(2L) and kk steps within the linearization radius,

    ‖Πu,μ​(wμ​(k)−wn,μ)‖2≥ηlr​g02​L​[1−(1−2​ηlr​L)k],\|\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}(k)-w_{n,\mu})\|_{2}\;\geq\;\frac{\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{0}}{2L}\bigl[1-(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}L)^{k}\bigr], (38)

    which grows monotonically and approaches g0/(2​L)g_{0}/(2L) geometrically.

  3. (iii)

    Bilateral suppression (A3): applying excision to both μ∈{v,t}\mu\in\{v,t\} simultaneously suppresses the Modality Anchor signal along unique directions to a residual term bounded by ϵanchor\epsilon_{\mathrm{anchor}}, so g0≤ϵanchorg_{0}\leq\epsilon_{\mathrm{anchor}} and the drift in (38) is at most ϵanchor/(2​L)\epsilon_{\mathrm{anchor}}/(2L).

Proof.

We analyze the gradient of the alignment loss ℒa\mathcal{L}_{a} with respect to the parameters of a single modality, and show that unilateral unlearning leaves a Modality Anchor signal from the unmodified branch that drives ρ\rho away from zero.

The cross-modal similarity s⁡(w)=zi,v​(wv)⊤​zj,t​(wt)s(w)=z_{i,v}(w_{v})^{\top}z_{j,t}(w_{t}) is an inner product of two vector-valued functions depending on disjoint parameter blocks. Let Jv​(wv)=∂zi,v/∂wv∈ℝm×dvJ_{v}(w_{v})=\partial z_{i,v}/\partial w_{v}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d_{v}} and Jt​(wt)=∂zj,t/∂wt∈ℝm×dtJ_{t}(w_{t})=\partial z_{j,t}/\partial w_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d_{t}} denote the Jacobians. By the inner product differentiation rule:

∇wvs​(w)=∇wv[zi,v​(wv)⊤​zj,t​(wt)]=Jv​(wv)⊤​zj,t​(wt),\begin{split}\nabla_{w_{v}}s(w)&=\nabla_{w_{v}}\bigl[z_{i,v}(w_{v})^{\top}z_{j,t}(w_{t})\bigr]\\ &=J_{v}(w_{v})^{\top}\,z_{j,t}(w_{t}),\end{split} (39)

where the cross term vanishes because zj,tz_{j,t} does not depend on wvw_{v}. By symmetry:

∇wts​(w)=Jt​(wt)⊤​zi,v​(wv).\nabla_{w_{t}}s(w)=J_{t}(w_{t})^{\top}\,z_{i,v}(w_{v}). (40)

Now consider the unilateral case where only wvw_{v} is unlearned. Suppose the projection and Forget Lock are applied to wvw_{v} only, producing wv∗w_{v}^{*}, while the language parameters remain at wn,tw_{n,t}. At the unlearned point w∗=(wv∗,wn,t)w^{*}=(w_{v}^{*},w_{n,t}), the alignment gradient with respect to wvw_{v} involves terms of the form

∇wvℒa∝Jv​(wv∗)⊤​zj,t​(wn,t),\nabla_{w_{v}}\mathcal{L}_{a}\;\propto\;J_{v}(w_{v}^{*})^{\top}\,z_{j,t}(w_{n,t}), (41)

where the proportionality absorbs the softmax weights from the InfoNCE loss. The critical observation is that zj,t​(wn,t)z_{j,t}(w_{n,t}) is the original textual embedding computed under the pre-unlearning parameters wn,tw_{n,t}, which encodes the full memory of the forgotten cross-modal alignment. This embedding acts as the Modality Anchor: during retraining, the gradient in Eq. (41) continuously pushes wvw_{v} toward directions that re-align zi,vz_{i,v} with the unchanged zj,t​(wn,t)z_{j,t}(w_{n,t}), thereby reconstructing the forgotten pairing and driving ρ\rho away from zero.

By an identical argument with the roles of vv and tt exchanged, if only wtw_{t} is unlearned to wt∗w_{t}^{*} while wvw_{v} remains at wn,vw_{n,v}, the alignment gradient with respect to wtw_{t} at the unlearned point w∗=(wn,v,wt∗)w^{*}=(w_{n,v},w_{t}^{*}) satisfies

∇wtℒa∝Jt​(wt∗)⊤​zi,v​(wn,v).\nabla_{w_{t}}\mathcal{L}_{a}\;\propto\;J_{t}(w_{t}^{*})^{\top}\,z_{i,v}(w_{n,v}). (42)

Here zi,v​(wn,v)z_{i,v}(w_{n,v}) is the original visual embedding, which serves as the Modality Anchor that pulls the language branch back toward the erased alignment during retraining, again yielding ρ>0\rho>0.

Now suppose both modalities are unlearned simultaneously, producing w∗=(wv∗,wt∗)w^{*}=(w_{v}^{*},w_{t}^{*}). The projection in Eq. (10) removes the unique-subspace components from both wvw_{v} and wtw_{t}, displacing both embeddings away from the original alignment. At the bilateral unlearned point, the alignment gradients become

∇wvℒa∝Jv​(wv∗)⊤​zj,t​(wt∗),\nabla_{w_{v}}\mathcal{L}_{a}\;\propto\;J_{v}(w_{v}^{*})^{\top}\,z_{j,t}(w_{t}^{*}), (43)
∇wtℒa∝Jt​(wt∗)⊤​zi,v​(wv∗).\nabla_{w_{t}}\mathcal{L}_{a}\;\propto\;J_{t}(w_{t}^{*})^{\top}\,z_{i,v}(w_{v}^{*}). (44)

Crucially, both zj,t​(wt∗)z_{j,t}(w_{t}^{*}) and zi,v​(wv∗)z_{i,v}(w_{v}^{*}) are now displaced embeddings that no longer encode the original cross-modal alignment. To formalize this, we verify that the projection removes the forget-specific components from both branches. For the visual side, Theorem C.7 gives:

Πu,v​(wv∗−wn,v)=0,\Pi_{u,v}\,(w_{v}^{*}-w_{n,v})=0, (45)

and the Forget Lock (Proposition C.6) maintains this condition throughout retraining. An analogous condition holds for the language side:

Πu,t​(wt∗−wn,t)=0.\Pi_{u,t}\,(w_{t}^{*}-w_{n,t})=0. (46)

Since the forget-specific knowledge resides in 𝒰v\mathcal{U}_{v} and 𝒰t\mathcal{U}_{t}, Eqs. (45)–(46) guarantee zero displacement along the forget-specific directions in both modalities. When only modality μ\mu is excised, the alignment gradient retains the original embedding of the unmodified branch:

∇wμℒa∝Jμ​(wμ∗)⊤​zμ¯​(wn,μ¯),\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}\;\propto\;J_{\mu}(w_{\mu}^{*})^{\top}\,z_{\bar{\mu}}(w_{n,\bar{\mu}}), (47)

which encodes the forgotten alignment and acts as a fixed Modality Anchor; whenever zμ¯​(wn,μ¯)z_{\bar{\mu}}(w_{n,\bar{\mu}}) has a non-zero component along the range of Jμ​(wμ∗)⊤J_{\mu}(w_{\mu}^{*})^{\top} restricted to 𝒰μ\mathcal{U}_{\mu}, one has g0>0g_{0}>0, establishing claim (i). When both modalities are excised simultaneously, the gradient instead depends on the displaced embedding:

∇wμℒa∝Jμ​(wμ∗)⊤​zμ¯​(wμ¯∗).\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}\;\propto\;J_{\mu}(w_{\mu}^{*})^{\top}\,z_{\bar{\mu}}(w_{\bar{\mu}}^{*}). (48)

Since Πu,μ¯​(wμ¯∗−wn,μ¯)=0\Pi_{u,\bar{\mu}}(w_{\bar{\mu}}^{*}-w_{n,\bar{\mu}})=0, the embedding zμ¯​(wμ¯∗)z_{\bar{\mu}}(w_{\bar{\mu}}^{*}) no longer encodes the forgotten pairing, removing the dominant Modality Anchor signal along unique directions. By Assumption A3 (Appendix C.1), the residual anchor gradient at the bilateral excised point is bounded by ϵanchor\epsilon_{\mathrm{anchor}}, i.e., g0≤ϵanchorg_{0}\leq\epsilon_{\mathrm{anchor}}, establishing claim (iii).

Drift lower-bound tendency (claim (ii)).

For the unilateral case, let d⁡(k)=Πu,μ​(wμ​(k)−wn,μ)d(k)=\Pi_{u,\mu}(w_{\mu}(k)-w_{n,\mu}) denote the unique-subspace drift after kk local SGD steps, with d⁡(0)=0d(0)=0 by the projection. The SGD update projected onto 𝒰μ\mathcal{U}_{\mu} satisfies d⁡(k+1)=d⁡(k)+ηlr​g​(k)d(k{+}1)=d(k)+\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g(k), where g⁡(k):=−Πu,μ​∇wμℒa​(wμ​(k),wn,μ¯)g(k):=-\Pi_{u,\mu}\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}(w_{\mu}(k),w_{n,\bar{\mu}}). At k=0k=0, g⁡(0)=−Πu,μ​∇wμℒa​(wμ∗,wn,μ¯)g(0)=-\Pi_{u,\mu}\nabla_{w_{\mu}}\mathcal{L}_{a}(w_{\mu}^{*},w_{n,\bar{\mu}}) with ‖g⁡(0)‖2=g0\|g(0)\|_{2}=g_{0}, giving the one-step drift lower bound

‖d⁡(1)‖2=ηlr​‖g⁡(0)‖2=ηlr​g0,\|d(1)\|_{2}\;=\;\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,\|g(0)\|_{2}\;=\;\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{0}, (49)

which requires only A1–A2.

For k≥2k\geq 2, we invoke Assumption A4 (directional alignment), which asserts that within the linearization radius the unique-subspace gradients remain sign-aligned with g⁡(0)g(0), so that ‖g⁡(k)‖2≥g0−2​L​‖d⁡(k)‖2\|g(k)\|_{2}\geq g_{0}-2L\|d(k)\|_{2} under A1 (the first term is the Modality Anchor signal at the excised point, and the 2​L​‖d⁡(k)‖22L\|d(k)\|_{2} term accounts for first-order smoothness deviation as wμw_{\mu} drifts). Taking norms of d⁡(k+1)=d⁡(k)+ηlr​g​(k)d(k{+}1)=d(k)+\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g(k) and applying this lower bound gives

‖d⁡(k+1)‖2≥(1−2​ηlr​L)​‖d⁡(k)‖2+ηlr​g0.\|d(k{+}1)\|_{2}\;\geq\;(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}L)\,\|d(k)\|_{2}+\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{0}. (50)

Since ηlr<1/(2​L)\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}<1/(2L), the contraction factor γ:=1−2​ηlr​L∈(0,1)\gamma:=1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}L\in(0,1). Unrolling from d⁡(0)=0d(0)=0:

‖d⁡(k)‖2≥ηlr​g0​∑s=0k−1γs=ηlr​g0​(1−γk)1−γ=g02​L​[1−(1−2​ηlr​L)k],\|d(k)\|_{2}\;\geq\;\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{0}\sum_{s=0}^{k-1}\gamma^{s}\;=\;\frac{\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}\,g_{0}(1-\gamma^{k})}{1-\gamma}\;=\;\frac{g_{0}}{2L}\bigl[1-(1-2\eta_{\mathrm{lr}}L)^{k}\bigr], (51)

which is Eq. (38) in the theorem statement. The drift grows monotonically in kk and approaches g0/(2​L)g_{0}/(2L) geometrically. Under bilateral excision, A3 forces g0≤ϵanchorg_{0}\leq\epsilon_{\mathrm{anchor}}, so the lower-bound tendency in Eq. (38) is suppressed to the scale of ϵanchor/(2​L)\epsilon_{\mathrm{anchor}}/(2L), removing the systematic reconstruction pressure present in the unilateral case. ∎

Appendix D Compute-Matched Retrain Comparison

A natural reviewer concern is whether the efficiency gains of EASE simply reflect a smaller training budget relative to retrain. To isolate budget from algorithmic contribution, we compare our method against retrain early-stopped at 25%25\%, 50%50\%, and 75%75\% of the full federated round count, alongside the full-budget retrain reference. The communication cost C​o​m​m.Comm. directly reflects the compute budget consumed, since per-round payload is constant within each scenario. Results on Flickr30K with CLIP-B/32 are reported in Table 4.

EASE uses less communication than Retrain-25%25\% in every scenario (Table 4) yet improves R​-​R​@​1R\text{-}R@1 by +24.2+24.2, +19.1+19.1, and +25.2+25.2 points on the client, class, and sample scenarios, respectively, while keeping forget-side metrics near the full-budget retrain reference. Retrain-25%25\% can also produce low forget recall, but its retain collapse indicates undertraining rather than targeted unlearning. EASE reaches retain quality close to Retrain-75%75\% at only 2020–25%25\% of the full communication budget.

Appendix E Likelihood-Ratio Attack at Low False-Positive Rate

We report LiRA​TPR​@​FPR=1%\mathrm{LiRA}~\mathrm{TPR}@\mathrm{FPR}{=}1\%, defined in Appendix B.4, across all nine (dataset, backbone) combinations and three unlearning scenarios in Figure 10, averaged over three seeds with standard-deviation error bars.

Cross-dataset pattern.

Across all nine combinations, EASE stays within 1.51.5 points of Retrain on every scenario, placing it consistently at the bottom of each subplot. In contrast, forget-reconstruction baselines such as Ferrari, FedOSD, and FUSED sit in the 2525–4242% range on the client and class scenarios, suggesting that their aggregate MIA values in Section 4.2 underestimate how much forget-side signal a targeted attacker can still recover. GradAscent produces the largest low-FPR leakage in the client scenario, consistent with the known instability of gradient-reversal updates on tightly coupled modalities.

Backbone sensitivity.

The relative ordering is stable across CLIP-B/32, CLIP-L/14, and SigLIP; absolute values shift upward for larger encoders (CLIP-L/14) due to greater capacity for memorization, but the gap between EASE and baselines widens rather than shrinks. This is consistent with bilateral excision targeting the Modality Anchor that scales with encoder capacity, while per-modality baselines do not close this anchor regardless of backbone size.

Scenario dependence.

The sample scenario produces uniformly lower TPR\mathrm{TPR} than client and class, because sample forget sets are sparsely distributed across clients and carry a weaker attacker signature in aggregate. Even so, our method approaches Retrain most closely in this regime, indicating that gains from bilateral excision persist even where the residual leakage is already small.
